cases.sentence: Берг, зять Ростовых, был уже полковник с Владимиром и Анной на шее и занимал всё то же покойное и приятное место помощника начальника штаба помощника ___ начальника штаба второго корпуса.
cases.explain: «первого отделения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Berg, the Rostóvs’ son-in-law, was already a colonel wearing the orders of Vladímir and Anna, and he still filled the quiet and agreeable post of assistant to the head of the staff of the assistant commander of the first division of the Second Army.

cases.explain: «второго корпуса» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Берг, в своих ___ на паре сытых саврасеньких, точно таких, какие были у одного князя, подъехал к дому своего тестя.
cases.explain: «аккуратных дрожечках» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Berg drove up to his father-in-law’s house in his spruce little trap with a pair of sleek roans, exactly like those of a certain prince. He looked attentively at the carts in the yard and while going up to the porch took out a clean pocket handkerchief and tied a knot in it.

cases.sentence: — Такое геройство вообще, каковое выказали ___, нельзя представить и достойно восхвалить!
cases.explain: «российские воины» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Altogether such heroism as was displayed by the Russian warriors cannot be imagined or adequately praised!” said Berg, glancing round at Natásha, and as if anxious to conciliate her, replying to her intent look with a smile. “ ‘Russia is not in Moscow, she lives in the hearts of her sons!’ Isn’t it so, Papa?” said he.

cases.sentence: — сказал Берг, оглядываясь на Наташу и как бы желая ее задобрить, улыбаясь ей в ответ на ее ___...
cases.explain: «упорный взгляд» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Altogether such heroism as was displayed by the Russian warriors cannot be imagined or adequately praised!” said Berg, glancing round at Natásha, and as if anxious to conciliate her, replying to her intent look with a smile. “ ‘Russia is not in Moscow, she lives in the hearts of her sons!’ Isn’t it so, Papa?” said he.

cases.sentence: — A y меня к вам, папаша, ___, — сказал он.
cases.explain: «большая просьба» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “And I have a great favor to ask of you, Papa,” said he.

cases.explain: «аглицким секретом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I was driving past Yusúpov’s house just now,” said Berg with a laugh, “when the steward, a man I know, ran out and asked me whether I wouldn’t buy something. I went in out of curiosity, you know, and there is a small chiffonier and a dressing table. You know how dear Vérushka wanted a chiffonier like that and how we had a dispute about it.” (At the mention of the chiffonier and dressing table Berg involuntarily changed his tone to one of pleasure at his admirable domestic arrangements.) “And it’s such a beauty! It pulls out and has a secret English drawer, you know! And dear Vérushka has long wanted one. I wish to give her a surprise, you see. I saw so many of those peasant carts in your yard. Please let me have one, I will pay the man well, and …”

cases.sentence: Граф с трубкой в руках ходил по комнате, когда Наташа, с изуродованным злобой лицом, как буря, ворвалась в комнату и ___ подошла к матери.
cases.explain: «быстрыми шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Berg was sitting beside the countess consoling her with the respectful attention of a relative. The count, pipe in hand, was pacing up and down the room, when Natásha, her face distorted by anger, burst in like a tempest and approached her mother with rapid steps.

cases.sentence: Граф утвердительно кивнул ей головой, и Наташа тем ___, которым она бегивала в горелки, побежала по зале в переднюю и по лестнице на двор.
cases.explain: «быстрым бегом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The count nodded affirmatively, and Natásha, at the rapid pace at which she used to run when playing at tag, ran through the ballroom to the anteroom and downstairs into the yard.

cases.sentence: В ___ тоже разнесся слух, что есть подводы, и на двор к Ростовым стали приходить раненые из других домов.
cases.explain: «соседних домах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The whole household, as if to atone for not having done it sooner, set eagerly to work at the new task of placing the wounded in the carts. The wounded dragged themselves out of their rooms and stood with pale but happy faces round the carts. The news that carts were to be had spread to the neighboring houses, from which wounded men began to come into the Rostóvs’ yard. Many of the wounded asked them not to unload the carts but only to let them sit on the top of the things. But the work of unloading, once started, could not be arrested. It seemed not to matter whether all or only half the things were left behind. Cases full of china, bronzes, pictures, and mirrors that had been so carefully packed the night before now lay about the yard, and still they went on searching for and finding possibilities of unloading this or that and letting the wounded have another and yet another cart.

cases.sentence: Наташа находилась в ___, которого она давно не испытывала.
cases.explain: «восторженно-счастливом оживлении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: They unloaded the wardrobe cart and sent it to take wounded men from a house two doors off. The whole household, servants included, was bright and animated. Natásha was in a state of rapturous excitement such as she had not known for a long time.
